Mission guide

Feedback group · playbook version 2

Your mission: help 30 people win back a healthier life

For eight weeks you’ll guide 30 people, each with a real problem like bad sleep or anxiety, as they use Aurelia. If they get better, and would miss it, Aurelia works. This guide is everything you need, in plain words.

New here? Start with these three things

1. What Aurelia isAn app where a person types one sentence about how they feel (“I can’t switch off at night”) and gets a personal audio session made for it, in about a minute. They listen, tap how they feel afterwards, and the next session (a “chapter”) adapts. That’s all a participant does.
2. What this study is30 real people with six common problems use Aurelia for eight weeks. You check in with them every day. At the end we know whether Aurelia actually helps.
3. Try it yourself firstBefore you talk to anyone, use Aurelia for three days with a problem of your own. You can’t guide people through something you haven’t felt.

Names and contact details for each role are confirmed before week 0 (see “Ready for week 0?”).

The mission in one minute

1They get betterThey move into the healthy range of their own questionnaire. That’s the win we’re here for.
2They keep coming backThree or more sessions a week, without being pushed harder each week.
3They’d miss itAt least 4 in 10 would be “very disappointed” to lose Aurelia.

What we believe: people with a common wellness problem who use Aurelia three times a week, with a little daily support from you, reach the healthy range of their problem within eight weeks, and would hate to lose it.

How we’d know we’re wrong (and that’s useful too): people don’t use it even with your support; or they use it and don’t change; or they change but wouldn’t miss it.

Your role

🧭 The guideAurelia makes the sessions and the chapters. You keep people listening and honest about how they feel. Tempted to give advice? Ask a question instead, and pass on what you hear.
📓 The keeper of the storyEvery contact goes in the coaching log the same day. If it isn’t in the admin, nobody can learn from it.
🛟 Not the doctorNever explain a score to a participant, never suggest stopping a treatment, never handle a crisis alone. Safety goes to the study lead the same day.

The six teams

Each person joins one team: the goal they pick in Aurelia’s onboarding, and one short questionnaire that measures it. Recruit to these numbers.

TeamGoal in the appMeasured withFinish line (healthy)A real step forwardPeople
Bad sleep → good sleepSleep betterInsomnia Severity Index (ISI), 0–287 or less6 points lower6
Anxious → calmFeel calmerGAD-7, 0–214 or less4 points lower6
Mental fog → clarityClear my mindPROMIS Cognitive Function45 or more5 points higher5
Low energy → energyMore energyPROMIS Fatigue54 or less5 points lower5
Distracted → focusedFocusPROMIS Cognitive Function45 or more5 points higher4
Stressed body → regulatedRegulate my bodyPerceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), 0–4013 or less4 points lower4

Everyone also answers WHO-5 (well-being, 0–100) every two weeks. A gain of 10 points is a real step; 28 or below means a person follows up with them. A clinical advisor confirms these lines before week 0.

How to read the table: Maya, in the sleep team (an example, not a real person)
  1. Week 0: her sleep questionnaire (ISI) scores 18. That’s moderate insomnia.
  2. Week 4: she scores 12. That’s 6 points lower: a real step forward. Tell the product team what’s working.
  3. Week 8: she scores 6. That’s 7 or less: she’s crossed the finish line. That’s a win.
You never have to calculate this yourself: the admin does it. And you never tell Maya her score means anything; that’s for the study, not for her.

NameWhat it asks aboutWho answers it
WHO-5Overall well-being: five short questions about the last two weeksEveryone, every two weeks
PHQ-9Low mood. Its last question asks about thoughts of self-harm, which is why it matters for safetyEveryone, weeks 0, 4 and 8

GAD-7How often anxiety shows upAnxious team

People fill them in inside the app; you only chase the ones that are late.

The journey: six levels in eleven weeks

−3 to −1
GatherW0
Day oneW1–2
HabitW3–4
HalfwayW5–7
Second halfW8–9
Finish

Questionnaires: WHO-5 at weeks 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8; their problem questionnaire and PHQ-9 at weeks 0, 4 and 8; interviews at weeks 0, 4 and 8; a quick check-in after every session. The admin works out every “made it” line for you in Experimentation → Milestones.

Level 0

Gather the team

Three weeks before week 0 · milestone M0

Find 30 people with six different problems, get their consent, and get the tools ready.

Your moves
  • Find 4–6 people for each of the six problems, from outside the team and outside anyone’s friends.
  • Check each person with a short mood questionnaire (PHQ-9) and the exclusion list in the study protocol. Anyone who can’t join gets pointed to support, never just dropped.
  • Take their consent and give each one a code name (P01–P30). Real names stay outside every tool.
  • Book every first call, and agree each person’s daily time (for sleep: the evening).
You’ve made it when
  • 30 people signed up, every group filled
  • Ethics review and clinical advisor have said yes

Stuck? Don’t start with fewer than 24. Recruit one more week rather than start a group with one person.

Level 1

Day one

Week 0 · milestone M1

Measure everyone before they start, and get them listening within two days.

Your moves
  • Collect WHO-5, their problem questionnaire and PHQ-9 before the first session. A “before” taken after is not a before.
  • First interview (30 minutes): what the problem feels like, what they’ve tried, what “solved” would mean to them.
  • Sit with each person for their first session: onboarding, their first sentence, the first play.
  • Write their goal sentence in the coaching log. It’s what you’ll cheer them towards for eight weeks.
You’ve made it when
  • Everyone has a “before” score (100%)
  • 9 in 10 played a first session in week 1

Stuck? Anyone without a “before” score doesn’t count for results. Get it before they play again.

Level 2

Build the habit

Weeks 1–2 · milestone M2

A daily rhythm: three or more sessions a week, a quick check-in after each.

Your moves
  • One short message a day, at each person’s time. Ask, don’t lecture.
  • Fewer than two sessions in a week? Call them: what got in the way, and one small change (shorter, earlier, another voice).
  • Write every contact in their coaching log, the same day.
  • Send WHO-5 at the end of week 2.
You’ve made it when
  • 7 in 10 did 3+ sessions in both weeks
  • WHO-5 answered by 85% or more

Stuck? Below 7 in 10, we’re measuring who had time, not whether Aurelia helps. Fix what’s in the way before week 3.

Level 3

Halfway check

Weeks 3–4 · milestone M3

See what’s working, and make one improvement for the second half.

Your moves
  • Week 4: WHO-5, their problem questionnaire, PHQ-9 and the second interview, with everyone.
  • Bring the three biggest findings to the product team, each with who it affects and their own words.
  • When the change ships, tell everyone in one message: what changed and why.
You’ve made it when
  • 85% still in
  • 85% of due questionnaires collected
  • The improvement has reached the group

Stuck? A disappointing week 4 isn’t a verdict. It’s exactly what the improvement is for.

Level 4

The second half

Weeks 5–7 · milestone M4

Check whether the improvement helped, and adjust once more if it didn’t.

Your moves
  • Keep the daily rhythm. People who are winning need less; people who are stuck need a call a week.
  • Send WHO-5 at week 6.
  • Follow up every safety alert the same day (the admin flags it for you), and write down what you did.
You’ve made it when
  • 6 in 10 stay regular (3+ sessions in 60% of weeks)
  • Every safety alert handled the same day

Stuck? If people drift off in the second half, ask them why on a call before changing anything else.

Level 5

The finish line

Weeks 8–9 · milestone M5

The final read, and the big decision: go, try again, or rethink.

Your moves
  • Week 8: WHO-5, their problem questionnaire, PHQ-9, “would you miss it?” and the third interview.
  • Write one story per group: where the person started and what changed, in their words, with their consent.
  • Present the result in week 9 against the finish lines set before week 0.
You’ve made it when
  • Half gain 10+ WHO-5 points
  • 4 in 10 reach a real improvement in their own problem
  • 7 in 10 still in
  • 85% of data collected
  • 4 in 10 would be “very disappointed” to lose Aurelia

Stuck? The finish lines were set before week 0. Moving them after seeing the data turns a study into a story.

A day in your shoes

08:30Open This week: calls first, then anyone you haven’t reached in two days, then missing questionnaires.
09:00–11:00Calls and follow-ups. Safety alerts always come first.
Their timeOne short message about their own goal (below).
Same dayLog it on their page: what they said, how they feel (1–5), the next step.
16:30Five-minute look at Wins and Engagement: who moved, who went quiet.

Your week

  • Monday: which level is next, and is it on track?
  • Wednesday: call everyone who did fewer than two sessions last week.
  • Friday: 30 minutes with the product team, the three biggest findings and who they affect.
  • Every other week: WHO-5 goes out; chase it within 48 hours.

The daily message

Bad sleep“Morning! How did last night go: roughly how long to fall asleep, and did you wake up?”
Anxious“How is your day feeling, 1 to 5? Did the session before your meeting help, or not really?”
Mental fog“Did you get a clear hour today? What did you play before it?”
Low energy“How was your energy this afternoon compared with yesterday?”
Distracted“How long did your longest focused stretch last today?”
Stressed body“Where do you feel it today? Did the breathing chapter change anything?”

One question, about their own goal, at the time they chose, on the channel you agreed with them (WhatsApp, SMS or email; it’s decided before week 0). Never “did you do your session?”.

What to say when…

They sayYou say
“Should I stop my sleeping pills / therapy?”“That’s one for your doctor. Aurelia isn’t a treatment and doesn’t replace one.”
“Is my score good?”“The scores are for the study, so I can’t read them for you. How do you feel it’s going?”
“The app keeps doing something annoying.”“Thank you, that’s exactly what we need to hear.” Then log it and pass it to the product team on Friday.
“I don’t have time this week.”“What if you tried a shorter one, at a different time?” One small change, no pressure.
Anything that worries you about their safetyStop coaching. Share crisis resources now. Tell the study lead the same day.

When someone drifts away

What happensWhat you do
Missed a dayYour usual message. No comment on the miss.
Not reached for 2 daysA second message, then a short call.
Fewer than 2 sessions in a weekA call: what got in the way, and one small change.
Two questionnaires missedA call, and offer to fill it in together.
Any sign of crisis or harmStop coaching. Crisis resources now, and the study lead the same day. Never alone.

Making Aurelia better, together

The study isn’t only a test. It’s how Aurelia gets better while people use it. One loop, every week:

Listen coaching log, interviews, check-insPick how many it hits × how much it stops themChange one change, on staging firstTell participants what changed and whyCheck same measures, before and after
  • At most one big change in each half (halfway, then once more if needed).
  • The questionnaires and their timing never change.
  • Every change is written down with the date it reached the group.

A great finding sounds like: “Four of six in the sleep team stop the session halfway because the voice is too fast (P02, P04, P05, P06; coaching log 3–5 Nov).” Who, how many, their words, where it’s written.

Your dashboard

Everything lives in admin → Experimentation. If a question isn’t answered there, tell the product team: that’s a gap in the tool, not a reason for a spreadsheet.

Today the admin shows sample data made by the same rules the real data will use, and the coaching log saves in your browser until the backend exists.

Words you’ll hear

Admin
The team’s website for running Aurelia. The study lives in its Experimentation section.
Coaching log
Your notes on each person, on their page in the admin.
Check-in
The quick “how do you feel now?” a person taps after each session.
Code name
P01–P30, used instead of real names everywhere.
Staging
The test copy of Aurelia where the product team tries a change before real participants see it.
Finish line
The healthy range of someone’s questionnaire, and the pass lines for week 9. Both are fixed before week 0 and never moved.
Regular
Three or more sessions in at least 6 of every 10 weeks.

The promises we always keep

Privacy
  • Code names (P01–P30) everywhere; real names stay outside every tool.
  • No names or contact details in the coaching log.
  • Journal and wearable data only with their own consent.
Safety
  • If someone answers anything other than “not at all” to the self-harm question in PHQ-9, scores 28 or less on WHO-5, or tells you about any harm: the study lead calls them the same day.
  • Crisis resources first, always.
  • Aurelia is not a treatment and never replaces one.
Honesty
  • Finish lines are fixed before week 0.
  • People who leave stay in the count.
  • We never claim Aurelia caused a change: there is no control group.

Week 9: the big moment

Go 🚀Most finish lines met, including “their own problem improves” and “would miss it”. Plan a proper trial and open a wider beta for the teams that won.
Try again 🔁People use it and stay, but results fall short. Another eight weeks on the same design, with the changes the data points to.
Rethink 🧭People don’t use it even with daily support, or wouldn’t miss it. Stop and rethink the core before building more.

Your first week on the job

  1. Day 1: use Aurelia yourself, with a real problem of your own. Keep going all week.
  2. Day 1: open admin → Experimentation and click through every tab with the sample data.
  3. Day 2: meet the study lead: safety process, crisis resources, how to reach them fast.
  4. Day 3: read Version 1 of this playbook once, including the protocol appendix. You don’t need to remember it, just know where things are.
  5. Day 4: agree with the product owner where to find participants, and the channel for daily messages.
  6. Day 5: walk through the checklist below and mark what’s missing.

Thirty people. Eight weeks. One question: does Aurelia help? You’re the person who finds out. Go win it for them.
